newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Rains seen boosting Bahia cocoa midcrop prospects.
newsitem.headline: Rains seen boosting Bahia cocoa midcrop prospects.

text.p: Rains in Brazil's key cocoa region of Bahia have helped raise expectations for the midcrop but even so the crop is still likely to be just over a million 60-kg bags, an official at a local processer said.

"Before expectations were between 700,000 and one million bags. Now with the rains, people are talking of between one million and 1.3 million bags although I think it is likely to be around 1.1 million bags," the official said.
"However that is nothing given 10 years ago we used to have midcrops of 2.6 million bags," he added.
The midcrop traditionally runs between May and September but this year began around two to three weeks late because of the impact of a prolonged dry spell during December and January.
Good rains since the middle of February have boosted production prospects however for the end of the midcrop when the bulk of the harvest is likely to take place.
"I reckon we will see 60 to 70 percent of the harvest coming in from the start of August," the processing official said.
Cocoa is trickling through currently from the start of the harvest but only very slowly, with prices around 24 reais ($22.43) per 15-kg arroba.
To make up for what is expected to be a 15,000 tonne shortfall between domestic demand and production, a pool of three companies is importing cocoa from Indonesia.
The first shipment of 4,000 tonnes has already arrived and a second vessel bringing 6,000 tonnes is due mid-July.
